chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, the knowledge that descended with Adam (عليه السلام) has not been raised, and knowledge is inherited. And Ali (عليه السلام) was the knowledgeable one of this community, and no knowledgeable one from among us has ever perished except that one from his family succeeded him who knew the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah willed.

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his family, indicating the familial line of succession
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: the divinely bestowed knowledge being discussed in the narration
key_terms.عَالِمَ: the knowledgeable authority or knower in the community
key_terms.مِثْلَ عِلْمِهِ: knowledge like his knowledge, expressing continuity of inherited knowledge
key_terms.نَزَلَ: descended from Allah, indicating revealed or God-given origin
key_terms.يُتَوَارَثُ: is inherited and passed from one rightful holder to another

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kafi describe the inheritance of divine knowledge through the Imams (عليهم السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the divine knowledge sent down from the time of Adam (عليه السلام) has remained present among humanity and is passed on by inheritance. It presents Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (عليه السلام) as the foremost bearer of knowledge in this Ummah and affirms the continuation of this knowledge through his family.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Knowledge is that which descended with Adam<sup>as</sup>. It has not been Raised (ever since). And the Knowledge is inherited, and It was so that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was a knowledgeable one of this community, and a knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup> from us<sup>asws</sup> does not pass away at all except he<sup>asws</sup> is replaced from his<sup>asws</sup> family, one<sup>asws</sup> who knows the like his knowledge, or whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ’Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and al-Fudayl from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The knowledge that came with Adam was not taken away. Knowledge is inherited. Ali (a.s.) was the knowledgeable person of this nation (Muslims). No one from us have ever left this world without leaving behind one like him in knowledge or what Allah wanted.”
